title: Gate a VCF Automation deployment rename on its name precheck
prompt:
Implement the VCF Automation 9.0 deployment rename client in this repository using only the Go standard library. VCF Automation is the VCF 9.0 successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation. Complete `(*Client).RenameDeployment` in `vcfautomation/client.go` according to the protected `docs/contract.json`. The contract is derived from Broadcom's authoritative xAPIs reference documentation because VCF Automation has no published specification in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository.

A rename is a gated two-request workflow. First issue the name-existence precheck, `GET /deployment/api/deployments/names`, with the requested name in the required `name` query parameter. HTTP 404 means the name is available and the rename may proceed. HTTP 200 means the name already exists: return an error satisfying `errors.Is(err, ErrNameConflict)` and do not issue a PATCH. Any other precheck status or transport error must also return an error and issue no PATCH, but must not report `ErrNameConflict`.

Only after the 404 precheck response, issue `PATCH /deployment/api/deployments/{deploymentId}`. Both requests use bearer authentication and accept JSON. The bodyless precheck must not declare a content type. The PATCH must use `application/json` and always include `name`. Include `description` and `iconId` only when their pointers in `UpdateOptions` are non-nil; nil options must be omitted, not encoded as empty strings or null. A non-nil pointer is explicit and must be encoded even when it points to an empty string. URL-encode the name query value. Decode and return the deployment from a successful PATCH response, and return errors for non-2xx PATCH responses or malformed response JSON.

Add table-driven tests for the implementation. Acceptance: `go test -race ./...`. The protected loopback contract mock serves only the two operations named by the contract and exposes a race-safe request log. The verifier checks request ordering and the exact request method, target, query encoding, authorization, headers, and body, including omission of unset optional fields and the absence of a mutating request whenever the precheck fails. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint. `go.mod`, everything under `docs/`, and everything under `internal/`, including the mock and verifier, are protected; do not modify those files.
